title: Hidden-state extraction
subtitle: The Inference Fabric's runtime has a single-pass hidden-state extraction mode with an empirical, fail-closed tensor-semantics detector.

stats.label: hidden-state extractions in one run through the broker
values per probe vector, up to 524,288 tokens per pass

lede: Inference Fabric was built for a distillation workload that needs a model's internal representation of every example, at dataset scale. Serving stacks return tokens, and running full generation to read one vector wastes the GPU. I added an extraction mode to the runtime itself, so the GPU spends nothing on tokens nobody needs. An engine built without a key-value cache routes to a raw TensorRT path that runs one forward pass per batch and returns the final hidden state of each sequence. A consumer has to pass a contract check before it may join the broker. At load the runtime enumerates every tensor the engine exposes.
quote: Validating vectors later cannot catch a well-formed vector for the wrong token.
evidence: Hidden-state extraction at scale: a single-pass TensorRT mode returning 4,096-value vectors, about 203,000 extractions over 10.8M tokens of a 7-billion-parameter FP8 model.
Fail-closed engineering: a warm-up probe that measures the engine's gather convention under both candidates and refuses to start on an ambiguous answer.
High-throughput batch inference: buffers bound once at maximum shape and a fixed shape, address and copy order, averaging 25,800 tokens per second with a peak of 45,500.
author: Corey James
